items.detail: The value it's compared with has a different type, so SQL Server converts customers.email on every row (`CONVERT_IMPLICIT(nvarchar(200),email,0) = @P1`) and can't seek the index. The usual cause is an application sending strings as nvarchar to a varchar column.
items.fix: Send the parameter with the column's exact type: VarChar instead of NVarChar (SqlDbType.VarChar in .NET, sql.VarChar in Node's mssql, a non-Unicode mapping in your ORM).
items.title: A type mismatch on customers.email stops SQL Server from seeking an index
items.verify: Explain again: no CONVERT_IMPLICIT in the plan, and the scan became a seek.

items.detail: The optimizer noticed it had to read shop.orders without a fitting index (1.0M rows read by Clustered Index Scan). Its estimate is a guide, not a promise: check the columns against the other queries on orders.
items.fix: Create the index on shipped_at and include total.
items.fix_sql:
CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [ix_orders_shipped_at]
    ON [shop].[orders] ([shipped_at])
    INCLUDE ([total]);
-- Add WITH (ONLINE = ON) on Enterprise or Azure SQL to keep the table available while it builds.

items.verify: Explain again: the suggestion is gone and the read of orders becomes a seek.

items.detail: The rows don't arrive in the order the GROUP BY / DISTINCT needs, so MySQL builds a temporary table (on disk once it outgrows tmp_table_size) and sorts the result.
items.fix: An index whose leading columns match the GROUP BY lets MySQL group in index order with no temporary table; ordering by an aggregate (COUNT(*) DESC) always needs a sort, so keep the grouped set small.
items.title: Collects 499K rows in an internal temporary table
items.verify: Explain again: no "using temporary table" on the grouping.
